newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, Italy meet on Alitalia, no comment.
newsitem.headline: EU, Italy meet on Alitalia, no comment.

text.p: Italian Industry Minister Claudio Burlando and EU Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock met on Friday for the second time in a month to try to pave the way for an agreement on Italy's rescue plan for flag carrier Alitalia.
But they both declined to make any comment to awaiting reporters after more than three hours of talks.
"They decided not to say anything," Kinnock's spokeswoman said, adding that the discussions were now in a "very sensitive and political" phase.

Italy last year requested EU permission for a capital injection worth some 3.3 trillion lire in the debt-ladden, state-controlled airline. Alitalia's managing director Domenico Cempella said last month that the Commission had suggested a reduction to 2.8 trillion lire.

Italy argues that the capital injection does not amount to state subsidies, but that it is acting in its right as a shareholder in the company -- a view which the Commission has rejected in many other airline rescue plans.

It usually subordinates its approval to strict conditions such a freeze in flights and fleet capacity and the adoption of a credible restructuring plan which ensures the company's long-lasting viability.
